correctness.rationale: For every \(D,r,L>0\) the first actual-reset depth transform follows uniquely from a two-region bounded Feynman-Kac equation and first-derivative matching, yielding \(q\kappa/(\kappa+s)\), and target-before-reset probability \(p\). Strong Markov renewal gives independent trials, \(N\) geometric, iid conditional exponential depths and the exact joint PGF-Laplace transform. Summing gamma densities proves the zero-atom/exponential mixture and moments, while direct weak-limit arguments prove the singular small-r and limiting large-r behavior. The resonant transform at \(s=\kappa\) is recovered by continuity. An independent exact Brownian-bridge-corrected trajectory simulation checks a grid of \(r\). The proof (not finite experiments) covers all positive parameters.

originality.rationale: The model, positive-rate constant mean cost and expected reset count are already in Tal-Friedman et al. Appendix C and Sec. II; no priority is claimed for them or for ordinary renewal methods. The separately checked contribution is the explicit state-dependent reset-depth transform, full joint law, mixed total-cost distribution, conditional reset-count law and singular cost fluctuations. Sunil et al. gives a joint-cost renewal scheme for unconditional resetting, not a covering evaluated one-sided transform. Plata et al. treats state-dependent resetting and MFPT without this reset-cost law. Relevant primary full texts and historical title/claim analogues were compared by implication; no equivalent evaluated result was found. Risk of an unlocated implicit/general method is acknowledged.

value.rationale: For the existing energy-efficient smart search model, mean total drag cost equals \(L\) irrespective of the monitoring rate, so mean-energy optimization hides cost risk. The exact full joint distribution gives observable-specific tail quantiles, the fraction of cost-free searches, a count conditioned on measured work, and \(\operatorname{Var}(C)=L^2+2L\sqrt{D/r}\), showing diverging risk from rare expensive trajectories at small r even as typical cost vanishes. These are natural full-path cost/risk observables tied directly to the source physical model, not an arbitrary moment or trivial parameter substitution. Scope remains idealized Brownian reset with linear distance cost.
